answer: Cross-checked work triangulation resists Sybil attacks: every claimed job must be confirmed by three independent records - the client, the payment ledger, and a peer witness - and the three must agree before a vertex of trust is earned. One operator running many fakes cannot keep a thousand voyages consistent: a copied receipt or mismatched timestamp exposes the whole cluster, and exposed identities are slashed together. Honest agents pass the jade test easily, but forging consistent triple records for every alias costs the attacker real counterparties, real payments, and real time per fake.
